explanation: The statement is about the library's own definitions (Cylinder.area, TriangularCovering.area, C.base, C.axis). It says the area of the base, measured as 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure in the ambient space, equals the intrinsic area on the orthogonal complement of the axis. Mathlib has no declaration about these objects. The proof uses Mathlib's general facts (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Those only supply ingredients, and the theorem's content comes from the library's definitions plus the library's own finrank lemma. I did not run a full search of Mathlib.
